links.comparator_used: Model reasoning on its own (unguarded) and model reasoning grounded by guideline retrieval, across nine frontier LLMs and 110 pharmacogenomic cases
links.outcome: Correctness and determinism of the pharmacogenomic phenotype/clinical mapping, and lethal-class errors
links.effect: Executing the validated versioned skill as code made the mapping exact and identical across models, and removed the ancestry gradient from the clinical mapping. Model-only reasoning was stochastic and unsafe. The abstract gives no numeric accuracy figures for this comparison.
links.tradeoff: All residual error remains at the single input-interpretation step. The ancestry gradient moves to the completeness of the input caller. The authors do not claim full clinical validation.
links.quote: Encoding the validated decision logic as a versioned skill and executing it as code made the pharmacogenomic mapping exact, auditable and identical across models, confining all residual error to a single input-interpretation step.

links.comparator_used: Model reasoning from its own knowledge without retrieval (also contrasted with the executed skill)
links.effect: Retrieval raised phenotype accuracy but increased lethal-class errors; the abstract gives no numbers.
links.tradeoff: Retrieval increased lethal-class errors, a new safety failure mode.
links.quote: Letting the model reason was stochastic and unsafe, and grounding it in the correct guidelines by retrieval paradoxically increased lethal-class errors.

design_hint: retrieval grounding vs executing validated decision logic as versioned code skill
